messages:
maria-dev: Heads up — saw multiple scale-up requests for eu-west GPU nodepools get stuck ~15m ago. CA logs show provisioning attempts but cloud API returning connection errors. Noticed downstream apps hit OOM/queueing. Anyone seen similar?

aj_sre: ops-bot flagged: "provisioner: rate limit hit (conn throttled)" around the same time. Could be cloud API 429s or control plane conntrack exhaustion.

devon-infra: Quick theory: when provisioner retries fast and many pools try to create nodes in-parallel we saturate control-plane -> LB or cloud API rate limits. CA default --max-node-provision-time=15m might be too low for spot pools that take longer.

tara-platform: Do we have warm-pools enabled for those GPU nodegroups? Warm pools staggered could avoid the burst. Also check --cloud-provider-backoff flags on the CA.

liam: sharing the flag set I prototyped on staging earlier today that helped under similar load:

```
--max-node-provision-time=30m
--scale-down-unneeded-time=15m
--scale-down-utilization-threshold=0.35
--expander=most-pods
--max-empty-bulk-delete=1
--cloud-provider-backoff=true
--cloud-provider-backoff-retries=8
--cloud-provider-backoff-duration=1s
```

maria-dev: tried bumping max-node-provision-time to 30m on staging and added backoff, reduced parallel creates. Staging showed fewer 429s but still saw a burst where the provisioner host ran low on ephemeral ports (short TCP TIME_WAIT recycle). Log snippet:

```
ERROR controller: failed to create instance: Post "https://cloudapi.example.com/v1/instances": dial tcp 10.11.12.13:443: connect: connection refused
WARN cloud: API returned 429 Too Many Requests, retrying (attempt=3)
netstat -an | grep TIME_WAIT | wc -l => 18k
```

ops-bot: [alert] provisioner: cloud-api-429 spike in eu-west (2026-03-19T14:02:11Z) :warning:

aj_sre: Action items I propose:
- avoid global burst: stagger warm-pool replenishment windows across AZs
- bump --max-node-provision-time for preemptible/spot pools to 30m (so CA doesn't mark as failed too quickly)
- enable cloud-provider-backoff and increase retries/duration to reduce thundering retries
- add runbook + prometheus rule to alert on cloud 429 rate and TIME_WAIT > threshold

devon-infra: Also consider expander change per workload. least-waste is good for packing but in mixed-gpu pools it can cause fragmentation and extra creates. most-pods reduced churn for us on staging.

maria-dev: Plan: 1) deploy flag change to dedicated eu-west CA replica set (staggered rollout), 2) create warm-pool with 1-2 warm nodes per AZ and a stagger window, 3) add cloud backoff flags, 4) monitor for 48h and revert if we see regression. I'll open PR with flags + short playbook.

tara-platform: I'll own the PR. pinging @aj_sre for rollback steps and validation checklist.

aj_sre: ack. add rollback to revert CA flags + scale warm-pool down, and include steps to temporarily route provisioning through alternate service account/region if cloud 429s persist. Also adding a note to incident runbook: "if cloud-429-provisioning persists > 30m, disable parallel create flows and rely on warm-pool until cloud recovers". :thumbsup:

maria-dev: thanks — I'll include the metric queries and example dashboards. We'll also capture a short perf delta for cold vs warm starts (tokens/sec, pod startup ms).

liam: one more nit: set --max-empty-bulk-delete=1 to avoid CA killing many empty nodes right after a surge — less oscillation.

maria-dev: good call. I'll include that. End of thread for now — will post PR link when ready. :rocket:
